objective: Compile the provider-originated Lumyn v3.1 update-delivery plan from confirmed change event through installed consumer policy, verified candidate, tested draft PR, and consented rollout status while keeping all runtime dispatch paused.
system_model_summary: The provider change plane supplies one confirmed non-executable contract and event. A revocable Consumer Installation owns event-specific repository, model-data, command, credential, delivery, and disclosure authority. The replaceable bounded model plane cannot self-approve or self-verify, and the status projection cannot infer consumer state.
proven_findings: The Go CLI, result envelope, init/check commands, schemas, and OpenAPI/docs intake have direct retained evidence.
Several recognized runtime commands are not implemented and may still return a generic pass until M0 closes.
The provider event, Consumer Installation, migration engine, verification ladder, local fallback export, tested draft PR, consented status projection, and paid campaign runtime are not implemented.
The external v2 Factory profile profiles/lumyn.yaml still represents the deterministic/PKI/receipt direction.
factoryd has not been qualified against v3 bounded-model, product-action, evidence, or closure semantics.

resolved.decision: Use a provider-paid update channel with services-assisted onboarding, a revocable Consumer Installation, deterministic transforms, and a replaceable bounded agent.
One Provider Change Contract is authoritative when accountably confirmed and reusable for the exact cohort; it and its provider event remain non-executable data and grant no repository authority.
Use deterministic verification independent from generation, preserve local fallback export, require a short-lived tested draft PR, and project only event-bound consumer-consented rollout status.

blocking: no implementation task has been separately approved
external Factory profile still encodes v2 for factoryd
factoryd v3 runtime qualification is absent

assumptions: Exactly 53 acceptance items and the authored M0-M10 graph are frozen.
Private consumer and commercial evidence remains outside the repository.
The coding agent is a replaceable adapter and explicit status-quo comparator.
unknowns: Exact external Factory profile change and version.
Exact factoryd qualification evidence and release.
constraints: No runtime implementation or live campaign dispatch in this generation.
No provider code access, production credentials, default-branch write, or auto-merge.

factory_compatibility.unblock_rule: No factoryd task dispatch until the external profile is updated and factoryd is qualified against the exact v3.1 control generation.

unblock_dependencies: Update external Factory profiles/lumyn.yaml to the approved v3.1 provider-originated update-delivery contract.
Qualify factoryd against this exact v3.1 task, installation, authority, bounded-model, delivery, status, evidence, and closure generation.
Re-run repo-pack self-test, repo-pack validation, and the full repository pre-push gate after both external dependencies are recorded.
factoryd_runtime.approval_posture: Factory approval never substitutes for exact private Lumyn product action authorization or human merge.
factoryd_runtime.credential_posture: no ambient consumer, provider, model, sandbox, or GitHub secrets
factoryd_runtime.network_posture: offline by default; exact task-scoped endpoints only

release_freeze.reason: Lumyn v3.1 Factory profile and factoryd runtime are not qualified.

runtime_pins.toolchain_version: go1.26.5; exact Node, npm, registry-or-snapshot, package-integrity, and toolchain pins before package-lock mutation
runtime_pins.dependency_policy: standard library first; pinned Go modules, parser runtime, model adapter, or tool dependency only with task evidence and license review
runtime_pins.distribution_target: explicitly licensed and integrity-signed design-partner binary or source package for consumer-local or consumer-controlled CI execution; public OSS, self-serve, and Homebrew require a separate approved gate
runtime_pins.provider_intent_policy: provider-originated API or SDK update delivery launched through a provider-paid, services-assisted sunset campaign; one accountably confirmed Provider Change Contract is reused by the exact invited cohort, each non-executable provider event binds its exact digest, audience, deadline, and supersession state, and neither contract nor event grants consumer repository authority; a universal registry, elaborate provider PKI, connection receipts, and receipt-backed billing are deferred
runtime_pins.model_policy: bounded agent use requires exact model provider, endpoint, model and version, parameters, prompt and tool digests, selected context and request-disclosure classes, retention and regional posture, credential environment and scopes, network endpoint and operations, read and write paths, file, line, diff, turn, token, time, retry, concurrency, attempt, and cost budgets, plus request, response, tool-call, usage, and patch provenance; the coding agent is replaceable, and repository, provider, tool, and model content is untrusted and cannot widen any boundary
runtime_pins.verification_policy: deterministic repository and workflow verification is independent from deterministic or agent-assisted generation, runs from the exact candidate head, preserves baseline failures, and cannot be satisfied by a model completion or self-verification
runtime_pins.delivery_policy: complete local evidence plus patch, optional local branch, and PR-ready bundle is the fallback; at least one tested draft PR requires separate short-lived non-default-branch and PR authorization, evidence-bound idempotency, and no auto-merge; manual delivery cannot close automated-delivery acceptance; provider status is event-bound, consumer-consented, provenance-labeled, and never inferred from silence
runtime_pins.artifact_namespace: .factory/artifacts contains source-safe Factory controls and separately consented aggregate or digest evidence only; consumer-private code, prompts, responses, patches, traces, credentials, and identifiable campaign evidence use an approved external private root
runtime_pins.live_work_policy: Factory worker capabilities are only approval, credentials, and network and never substitute for Lumyn product action scopes; consumer installation, event-specific authorization, model disclosure, model network, model credential, repository, command, registry, sandbox, GitHub, reporting, retention, and deletion actions are separate, expiring, revocable, fail-closed product grants
runtime_pins.dispatch_policy: factoryd dispatch is paused and fail-closed until the external profiles/lumyn.yaml contract is updated for v3.1 and factoryd is qualified against this regenerated task, authority, model, evidence, and closure generation
